title: bug: a required check command of 501-1000 characters passes validation but record_check_dispatch and record_check_run refuse it (500 cap)
description: validators.ts MAX_REQUIRED_CHECK_COMMAND_CHARS and guest-supervisor.py MAX_CHECK_COMMAND allow 1000 characters, but checkObservationStore.ts:78 and checkRunStore.ts:46 (and the record_check_dispatch/record_check_run schemas) cap the recorded command at 500, so a valid long command can be approved and run but never recorded. Use one shared limit.
definitionOfDone: Every daemon and guest limit on a required check command is the same value from one constant, with a boundary test at the limit and one past it on each path.

implementationPlan.description:
Align the declared tool contracts after both storage prerequisites ad5be1cf and d88bb990 land. Canonical value is the existing validators.MAX_REQUIRED_CHECK_COMMAND_CHARS=1000; do not lower required-check definitions/guest limits to500. Import that existing constant in recordCheckDispatch.ts and recordCheckRun.ts. Set command schema maxLength to it and interpolate its value in descriptions instead of stale500 prose:
```ts
command: {
  type: 'string',
  maxLength: MAX_REQUIRED_CHECK_COMMAND_CHARS,
  description: `The command, stored verbatim; non-blank, at most ${MAX_REQUIRED_CHECK_COMMAND_CHARS} UTF-16 code units.`,
}
```
Retain each tool's non-execution/provenance wording and all current required fields/runner-only authorization. Error handling remains store validation: no trimming, truncating, coercing or normalizing command bytes. All daemon runtime length checks and schema declarations now import this single canonical constant; prerequisites own store code/docs. Do not touch 500-character protected-path limits or10000-character completion verification limits.

In requiredChecks.test.ts add mutation-resistant schema/handler boundary tests using existing ToolTestHarness, validators and tool factories. Pin submitPlan requiredChecks command maxLength and both recording tool maxLength to the imported constant and explicit expected1000. Accept500,501 and1000; reject1001. Keep blank/non-string/control behavior unchanged on each path. Supplementary Unicode counts by UTF16: 500 emoji=1000 accepted, plus one ASCII unit rejected. Keep leading/trailing whitespace within the bound verbatim; do not trim to sneak1001 through. For record_check_dispatch invoke handler with its actual ToolCallContext.runner, approved revisions and current candidate; don't bypass auth. Record_check_run gets existing valid candidate/tree/source/runner fixture. Assert rejection before file/map writes. Preserve original tests, adjusting only obsolete cap expectations where relevant.
implementationPlan.note: Both record tool schemas now import validators.MAX_REQUIRED_CHECK_COMMAND_CHARS: command maxLength = constant, descriptions say 'at most 1000 UTF-16 code units'. Schema pin test + handler boundary tests added in requiredChecks.test.ts (snapshot run: 129 passed). Dirty peer paths (CI yml, scripts/*, .moe/tasks) untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
Own final cross-layer integration for this split. Add a required-check definition at1000 units, approve through existing submitPlan binding fixture, then create a valid attempt/current candidate using the existing state APIs from checkObservationStore.test.ts (read-only reference), dispatch it through recordCheckDispatchTool and record its authenticated observation via recordCheckObservation. Assert persisted/reloaded CheckRun.command equals the approved bytes and1001 never reaches storage. Also cover direct legacy recordCheckRunTool at boundary without upgrading its declared provenance. No production import changes beyond the two schemas.

Pin the existing standalone Node/Python mirrors behaviorally against the SAME imported canonical daemon constant: import guest-bridge.mjs checkFrame from the repo scripts via test-only dynamic import; feed identical boundary/emoji/whitespace strings into it and actual guest-supervisor.py read_check using an isolated python3 -I -B subprocess, following local-runner-check.test.mjs C2's length-prefixed frame batching. Manually frame rejected inputs so Python checks them too. Assert m.MAX_CHECK_COMMAND equals the daemon constant, and both runtimes accept limit/reject limit+1. This is one canonical logical limit with test-enforced cross-language mirrors, not a runtime TS import in the standalone guest; no new packaging asset/generator. Linux/WSL must execute Python cases; native Windows may explicitly skip only guest-dependent cases, not the daemon/tool tests. Close subprocess pipes, use bounded timeout/maxBuffer, and assert diagnostics on failed subprocess rather than silently skipping it. Tests must not execute the command strings or start a VM.
